cells.tense: You are here with it, and what you see arrives before you've reached for words.
cells.ask: Take one thing your practice has made clear and say it to someone plainly, once, without softening the edges.
cells.core:
You can hold more than one true thing at a time and stay steady while you do. That comes from doing the same work long enough that it starts to speak for itself. You feel the difference between something you've tested and something that merely sounds good, and you feel it fast.

What's waiting now is the moment you set it down where someone else can hear it. No rehearsal about how they'll take it. Nothing to settle first. You already see the thing; saying it plainly is the next step the work has been pointing at. You don't need their reaction to know whether it's true.
cells.sheetLine: You see it clearly. Say it where it can be heard.
cells.verb: holding many truths at once and letting what you see sort them
cells.place: a small steady practice, kept lit by repetition

cells.tense: You are bracing for what comes after this, already turning what you see into a case to win.
cells.ask: Do one thing the same way tomorrow as today — no adjusting, no extra effort, no checking whether it's working.
cells.core:
You're running ahead of where you actually are. What you perceive is real, and you've started spending it on preparation — the version of this you'll need when it counts. What was quiet attention has become rehearsal. The repetition that built the skill now spends its time checking whether the skill is enough.

That's the bend: not what you see, which lands fine, but how far forward you're living inside it. Certainty gets used up when it's aimed at a future you can't write in yet. Put the practice back where it belongs — the thing you do today, at the size it actually is. Nothing needs settling before tomorrow's version of it.
cells.sheetLine: What you see is real. You're aiming it past where you stand.
cells.verb: holding many truths at once and letting what you see sort them

cells.tense: You have what's worth saying and you stopped handing it over, and that stillness still holds you.
cells.ask: Tell one person something your practice has taught you, without needing it to be useful or well received.
cells.core:
You can hold many truths and you do. What has gone quiet is offering them. The work continues — you sit with it, you refine — but what comes out stays in the room with you. You watch other people say what you already see and you don't join in. Not because you've stopped noticing. Because staying quiet got comfortable enough to feel like the shape of you.

What's starved is the line out, the move that carries what you find toward someone else. Without it, you turn it over and over and it settles. You don't need to trust how it will land. One person, one thing you've come to know, said for no better reason than that it's true.
cells.sheetLine: You keep what you know, and it isn't moving anymore.
cells.verb: holding many truths at once and letting what you see sort them

cells.tense: You are already reading what's true in the room and crediting something other than yourself for it.
cells.ask: Name one thing you already think about a situation you're in and say it as yours — out loud, without calling it instinct, luck, or a feeling.
cells.core:
It runs right now — the fast read of what matters and what doesn't — and it's usually right. But you pass it off. Something landed, you had a feeling, the work showed you. As if the clarity came from somewhere else and only visited. The practice didn't build that. It sharpened what was already yours.

Nothing about what you notice has to change. The credit is the open question. Handing it to a mood or a process makes it weigh less than it should, and you know that when you hear yourself do it. Say the next one in your own name. Same read, same accuracy, standing under it as the one who saw.
cells.sheetLine: You see it and call it borrowed. Say it as yours.
